healthPage.title: What can a walk in nature do for you?
healthPage.intro: Walking is no miracle cure, but it is a simple way to get moving, spend time outside and give your mind a little room. Here is what research can tell us with reasonable confidence.
healthPage.minuteLabel: of moderate activity per week is a benchmark for adults.
healthPage.minuteNote: According to the World Health Organization; every bit of movement counts.
healthPage.factsIntro: The science of nature and well-being is growing. The results are promising, but not magical — which is good news: it is fine to start small.

facts.title: Movement helps your mind too
facts.text: Regular physical activity is associated with better mental well-being, sleep and cognitive health. A brisk walk can be more than simply getting from A to B.

facts.title: Nature adds something extra to your walk
facts.text: A recent review brought together 57 studies and found that being active in natural settings can strengthen mental well-being. Woodlands, meadows and water are wonderful allies for time outdoors.

facts.title: Enjoyment is a powerful ally
facts.text: Research on green exercise often finds more enjoyment and a more positive short-term feeling. A route you want to choose again is a great place to start.

healthPage.tryTitle: Make your next walk a mini-break
healthPage.tryText: No performance, no stopwatch. Choose one small focus and let the route do the rest.
trySteps: Choose a route that suits the time you have today.
Notice three things along the way that you had not seen before.
Walk at your own pace and notice how you feel afterwards.
healthPage.tryAction: Choose a walk on the map
healthPage.sourcesTitle: Where do these insights come from?
healthPage.sourcesIntro: This page draws on authoritative guidelines and systematic reviews. These bring together results from several studies and also highlight uncertainties.
healthPage.disclaimer: Walking can be a valuable addition, but it is not a substitute for professional support with mental-health concerns.
